newsitem.title: CANADA: Rate cuts offset lower revenues - Canada's Martin.
newsitem.headline: Rate cuts offset lower revenues - Canada's Martin.

text.p: Canada's Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Wednesday that lower government revenues would be offset largely by lower interest payments in the current and the next fiscal years.

For fiscal 1996/97 ending March 31, budgetary revenues are expected to be C$1.6 billion lower than projected in Martin's March 1996 budget. Program spending is anticipated to be C$0.3 billion lower, and much lower interest rates have lowered estimated public debt charges by C$1.3 billion.

For 1997/98, budgetary revenues are expected to be C$1.9 billion lower than forecast in the March budget. But program spending would be C$0.4 billion lower and public debt charges C$1.5 billion lower.
The net result is an unchanged deficit target for both years. The figures were included in the economic and fiscal update made by Martin today to the House of Commons finance committee.
He said that for planning purposes, the employee unemployment insurance premium rate in 1997 was assumed to be C$2.90 for every C$100 of insurable earnings, the same as in the March budget.
